# Multi-org GitHub App

One GitHub App, installed on several GitHub orgs, lets a single agent work across all of them as one bot identity. This page covers how it works, operator setup, the org-admin install steps, the admin status card, and troubleshooting. Env var reference: [`configuration-agent.md`](https://github.com/app-vitals/shipwright/blob/main/docs/configuration-agent.md); file map: [`agent-key-files.md`](https://github.com/app-vitals/shipwright/blob/main/docs/agent-key-files.md).

With a single installation, behavior is identical to a one-org setup. Per-owner token files are always written under App auth, even with one installation; PAT auth writes none.

## How it works

- **Discovery.** The agent signs an App JWT from `GH_APP_ID` + `GH_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` and lists the App's installations. It keeps those whose owner appears in the agent's repo scope (`org/repo` entries). `GH_APP_INSTALLATION_ID`, if set, is an optional pin: it is always used, and wins over a discovered installation for the same owner.
- **Default installation.** The pin if set, otherwise the lowest selected installation id. Its token is written to the `gh-token` file, so single-installation behavior is unchanged.
- **Per-owner tokens.** Under App auth, each usable installation's owner token is also written to `gh-token.d/<lowercase-owner>` next to `GH_TOKEN_FILE` (atomic write, mode 0600). The directory is kept even with a single installation; owners that are no longer usable are pruned. Under a PAT nothing is written there.
- **Routing.** Under GitHub App auth every `gh` and git command must carry `SHIPWRIGHT_GH_OWNER=<org>`; the `gh` wrapper and the git credential helper read `gh-token.d/<lowercase-owner>` for that org. The hint is not inferred from `-R`, API paths, clone arguments, the request path or the working directory. An unset hint fails with a message explaining the variable and the retry form (stderr only; expected for DMs). A hint with no token file fails naming the org and pointing at the admin GitHub Installations card; it never falls back to another org's token or the default one. Under PAT auth the hint is ignored.
- **Where the hint comes from.** Loop dispatches (dev-task, review, patch, deploy) carry the owner of the task or PR's repo. Cron runs carry the default org (the pinned installation, else the lowest installation id). Slack DMs carry no hint, because a DM is not tied to an org: prefix each command with `SHIPWRIGHT_GH_OWNER=<org>` yourself. That prefix is also the per-command override for any run. [`RUNTIME.md.template`](../runtime/workspace/RUNTIME.md.template) teaches the agent this rule.
- **Re-sync.** Discovery re-runs on the agent's config-sync tick (every 60 seconds), so scope changes and new installs are picked up without a restart.
- **Broken installations.** An installation is marked broken when GitHub reports it suspended or rejects the token mint (403, 404 or 422). Transient errors (5xx, network) are logged and retried, not marked broken.
- **Repo name collisions.** Repos clone to `repos/<repo>` regardless of owner, so two scoped repos with the same name under different orgs collide. Admin rejects such a repo list with a 400; the clone sync skips the later repo.
- **No PAT regression.** App auth engages only when a pin exists or discovery finds at least one usable installation. Otherwise the agent stays on the PAT path.

## Operator setup

Everything is env-var only:

| Variable | Required | Notes |
|----------|----------|-------|
| `GH_APP_ID` | yes | The App's id. |
| `GH_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` | yes | PEM key; `\n`-escaped newlines are accepted. |
| `GH_APP_INSTALLATION_ID` | no | Pin one installation as always-used and default. Omit to rely on discovery. |
| `GH_APP_SLUG` | no | The App's URL slug. Set automatically by the admin manifest flow; needed for the "Add another org" link. Set it by hand when using an existing App. |

Then add each org's repos to the agent's repo scope.

### Creating the App from admin

The admin "Set up GitHub App (auto)" action has an **Installable on multiple orgs (public App)** checkbox, off by default. Check it for an App that will be installed on orgs other than its owner. The manifest flow stores `GH_APP_SLUG`, and the installed callback no longer overwrites an installation id that is already stored.

### Using an existing private App

A private App can only be installed on its owning account. To make it installable elsewhere, open the App's settings on GitHub and use **Make public** (Advanced). This was verified against a throwaway App: existing installation ids and token minting are unchanged by the flip, and other accounts can install the App afterwards.

## Org-admin install steps

1. From the agent's detail page in admin, use **Add another org** (shown once `GH_APP_SLUG` is set), or open `https://github.com/apps/<slug>/installations/new`.
2. Pick the target org, then choose all repositories or the specific ones the agent needs. The person installing must be an owner of the org, or request approval from one.
3. Wait up to 60 seconds. The next config-sync tick discovers the installation; no restart or env change is needed, provided the org's repos are in the agent's scope.

Once the first install exists, no admin provisioning session is needed to complete an additional-org install.

## Admin status card

The agent detail page shows a **GitHub Installations** card with one row per installation: owner, state, and last error. The agent reports its state to admin (`PUT /agents/:id/github-installations`, see [`agent-api-resources.md`](./agent-api-resources.md#github-installations-snapshot)) when it changes and on a 30-minute heartbeat. Reports never include tokens or keys. Admin only displays the snapshot; it never calls GitHub or the agent.

| State | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| in scope / ok | Token minting works. |
| discovered, not in scope | The App is installed on the org but none of the agent's repos are. |
| pinned | The `GH_APP_INSTALLATION_ID` installation. |
| broken | Suspended, or the token mint was rejected. The last-error column says which. |

A stale warning appears when the last report is more than 90 minutes old (three missed heartbeats).

## Signed commits

Commits pushed with plain git are unsigned. Under App auth an agent can instead land commits that GitHub signs, so they show **Verified**.

- **Enable.** Set `SHIPWRIGHT_SIGNED_COMMITS=1` in the agent's env. It is off by default, and any other value (e.g. `off`) is off. In admin, the agent detail page's Agent Policy card has a **Signed commits** checkbox, shown only when the agent has `GH_APP_ID` set. Checking it upserts the env row; unchecking deletes it.
- **Git wrapper.** `scripts/bin/git` sits ahead of real git on `PATH`. With the flag on it routes `git push` through `scripts/signed-push.ts`, which replays the local commits not yet on the remote (topological order) through the REST Git Data API using the per-owner installation token: per commit it creates a tree, then a commit (with no author/committer, so GitHub signs it), verifies the signature, and finally moves the branch ref once all commits are created. It verifies the remote tree matches local `HEAD^{tree}`, then syncs the worktree with `git fetch` and `git reset --mixed` (uncommitted work survives). Merge commits keep every parent; root commits and unrelated history are fine. Every other subcommand, and push with the flag off, execs real git unchanged. Global options (`-C`, `-c`) are honored.
- **Owner hint.** Like the `gh` wrapper, an intercepted push needs `SHIPWRIGHT_GH_OWNER=<org>` to pick the org token. Unset gives a teaching error; retry with it prefixed.
- **PAT auth.** With no `GH_TOKEN_FILE` (or the file missing) there is nothing to sign with, so push passes through to real git.
- **Refusals.** Some pushes cannot be reproduced exactly through the REST API, so the helper exits non-zero instead of silently differing: force/tag/delete pushes and oversized commits (default 10 MB base64 per commit, override with `SHIPWRIGHT_SIGNED_COMMITS_MAX_BYTES`; GitHub documents no real limit, so tune it if one is observed). Merge commits, mode changes, symlinks, submodules, root commits, and unrelated history are all supported. Non-fast-forward pushes are no longer refused; they behave like regular git push (print git's standard rejection message).
- **Bypass.** Every refusal ends with the fix: prefix that one push with `SHIPWRIGHT_SIGNED_COMMITS=off`, e.g. `SHIPWRIGHT_SIGNED_COMMITS=off git push origin my-branch`. That push is unsigned.
- **SHAs change.** The API re-creates each commit, so local SHAs differ after a push; the local branch is moved to the new head. Anything that recorded a pre-push SHA (notes, PR comments) is stale.
- **Partial failure.** The remote branch only moves once, after every commit is created and the tree check passes. A failure before that changes nothing on the remote or in the worktree, so fix the cause and re-run the push.

## Troubleshooting

- **`SHIPWRIGHT_GH_OWNER is not set` from `gh` or git.** Expected in DMs. Retry with the hint prefixed, e.g. `SHIPWRIGHT_GH_OWNER=<org> gh pr list -R <org>/<repo>`. If a loop or cron run hits it, check the agent logs for a `[spawn-env]` warning: no owner could be resolved for that spawn.
- **A new org does not show up.** Allow 60 seconds. Confirm the org's repos are in the agent's scope and the App is installed on that org (not just authorized).
- **"discovered, not in scope".** Add at least one repo from that org to the agent's repo scope.
- **`gh wrapper: no GitHub App installation token for org '<org>'`.** The installation is missing, broken, or not yet picked up. Check the card, then the install on GitHub.
- **Broken: installation suspended.** Unsuspend it in the org's installed-Apps settings.
- **Broken: token mint rejected.** The installation was removed or its permissions were revoked. Reinstall it.
- **Admin rejects the repo list (400).** Two repos share a name across orgs. Scope only one of them.
- **Card is stale or missing.** The agent may be down or unable to reach admin. A missing card means no snapshot was ever reported.
- **Agent still uses a PAT.** App auth did not engage: no pin and no usable in-scope installation. Check `GH_APP_ID`, the key, and the card.
- **`signed-push: refusing`.** The push has something the commit API cannot express. Read the reason; use the printed `SHIPWRIGHT_SIGNED_COMMITS=off git push ...` bypass if an unsigned push is acceptable.
